t: Introduction and overview — Tarawa-class Amphibious Assault Ship
name: Introduction and overview — Tarawa-class Amphibious Assault Ship — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Tarawa-class Amphibious Assault Ship
description: Introduction and overview of the Tarawa-class Amphibious Assault Ship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Tarawa class — five ships — were the first U.S. LHAs, combining the capabilities of four older amphibious ship types into 39,400-ton hulls. Tarawas introduced the well-deck-plus-flight-deck LHA concept later perfected by the Wasp class. The last retired in 2015; two await disposal or foreign transfer. Baseline facts: U.S. amphibious assault ship; 5 built; first LHA; 39,400 tons..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
key_points: Tarawa-class Amphibious Assault Ship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history.
U.S. amphibious assault ship; 5 built; first LHA; 39,400 tons.
